messages.subject: model not initializing as expected
parts: Hi. I am running into unexpected behavior when trying to initialize a model. I have attached a zip file containing a script, my model code, and an R workspace loaded by the script. When I initialize the model in the attached, the node "psi" is not getting populated with the values in the list of initial values I am sending to `nimbleModel`. Wondering if anyone help me spot my problem.

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: model not initializing as expected
parts:
Quresh, this is a great question, and a subtle point of nimble.  Let me try to explain.

When you define psi, as you do using a transformation on the lefthand-side:

logit(psi[i, t]) ~ dnorm(.....)

under the hood, nimble *changes* your model code to instead be exactly the following:

logit_psi[i, t] ~ dnorm(.....)
psi[i, t] <- ilogit(logit_psi[i, t])

Then, you provide an initial value for psi.  When the model is built, logit_psi[] is populated with NA's (since no initial value is provided for logit_psi), and the elements of psi[] are populated with the initial value you provide.

Then, nimble tries to calculate values (and log-densities in the model).  Working "downwards" in the graph of model dependencies, first the log-densities of logit_psi are calculated, which are all NA (since logit_psi is all NA's), then the value of psi[] is calculated, which is a deterministic calculation of logit_psi (currently NA's), so psi is now replaced with ilogit(NA), which is NA.

So, the quick fix is to, in your initial values list, change the name "psi" to "logit_psi", and in the values associated with this, replace it with logit(previous_initial_values).

I, myself, would also rewrite the model for more clarity, to avoid the lefthand-side transformation, and thus allowing you to name the variables whatever you want, rather than relying on nimble to modify the code for you.

Let me know if this fixes your problem.

Cheers,
Daniel
